_about: Hand-transcribed, machine-readable snapshot of the Daikin One Open API contract. Source of truth for tests. Everything here comes from the two published pages; anything the pages do not state is listed under 'undocumented' rather than guessed.

rules: heatSetpoint must be lower than coolSetpoint by at least setpointDelta
both setpoints must be between setpointMinimum and setpointMaximum
a successful request turns off schedule and away state
away state takes priority over schedule
unitary systems only; VRV (P1P2) and single/multi-split (S21) run the fan at maximum speed

http_status.400: Bad request - problem with the request parameters, see response body
http_status.401: Unauthorized - the accessToken is not valid
http_status.403: Forbidden - the integratorApiKey is not valid
http_status.415: Unsupported Media Type - Content-Type is not application/json
http_status.429: Too Many Requests - rate of API calls is too high

error_body.note: The error body key is documented as 'messages' (plural); the success body key on writes is 'message' (singular).

messages.Success: Request is sent to the thermostat

modeEmHeatAvailable.note: if available, mode may equal 4 (emergency heat)

fan.note: described as 'System fan'; 'refer to fanCirculate for fan settings'

geofencingEnabled.note: appears in the GET /v1/devices/<id> example only; has no row in the data definitions table

undocumented: Unit of accessTokenExpiresIn, and any refresh mechanism other than calling POST /v1/token again.
Whether a 429 response carries a Retry-After header.
Which HTTP status accompanies DeviceOfflineException, and whether GET /v1/devices/<id> returns it for an offline thermostat or only writes do.
The 'Status field in the response body' mentioned in the HTTP Responses prose; no such field appears in any documented body.
equipmentStatus 0, which the example response uses but the enum does not define.
The meaning of modeLimit 0 ('none') as distinct from 1 ('all').
Whether the 3-minute polling limit is per thermostat or per account.
Whether 'fan' reports the fan setting or whether the fan is running.
Whether /msp enforces setpointDelta in heat-only or cool-only mode, where one setpoint is inactive.
Away state and geofencing are mentioned but have no read field (away) or write endpoint (either).

page_source_hints_not_part_of_contract.note: These sit inside an HTML comment in the documentation page source. They are not published contract and the integration must not depend on them, but they show that values outside 1-5 can plausibly be returned.

observed_live._about: Differences between the published documentation and real responses, from the read-only live check. The documentation above is left as published; this section records what the service actually does.
observed_live.thermostat: Daikin One Touch, model string 'ONETOUCH', firmware 4.0.17, unitary system

token.note: An integer; consistent with seconds (15 minutes). Response keys match the documentation.

get_device.modeEmHeatAvailable: Sent as a JSON boolean (false), not the documented integer 0/1. The client accepts both.

extra_fields.equipmentCommunication: integer; undocumented, meaning unknown, not used by the integration

get_device.number_types: Whole-number values of float fields arrive as JSON integers (for example setpointMinimum 10, tempIndoor 24).
get_device.equipmentStatus: 5 (idle) observed; 0 from the documented example was not seen.

not_observed: An offline thermostat, so the status code and endpoint behavior for DeviceOfflineException remain unknown.
HTTP 429, so whether Retry-After is sent remains unknown.
A /msp write that changes the mode, one sent while the schedule is on, and one that violates the limits or delta.
observed_live.set_mode_setpoints: Two rounds of PUT /v1/devices/<id>/msp on both thermostats in heat mode (heat setpoint 23.3 -> 21.1 -> 23.3, mode and cool setpoint resent unchanged) returned HTTP 200. A read 15 seconds later returned exactly the values sent.
